findings.title: A death the field search misses — SureForm 30 gray reload
findings.headline: 24 reports, 0 deaths — until you read the narrative
findings.brief: A MAUDE search for model number 48230M returns 24 reports and zero deaths, yet report 2955842-2026-01596 describes a fatal event during a robotic pulmonary lobectomy when the SureForm 30 stapler (model 488530-13) fired on the pulmonary artery with no error message. “IT APPEARED THAT NO STAPLES WERE APPLIED TO THE PA. THE STAPLER WAS REMOVED AND MASSIVE BLEEDING OCCURRED … DESPITE OPENING AND RESUSCITATION EFFORTS, THE PATIENT EXPIRED IN THE OPERATING ROOM.” The report was received eight weeks before Intuitive’s 11 March 2026 recall of the 8 mm SureForm 30 gray reloads, and the product number 48230M appears only in the free‑text field D10 of that report.

spotlight.quote: IT APPEARED THAT NO STAPLES WERE APPLIED TO THE PA. THE STAPLER WAS REMOVED AND MASSIVE BLEEDING OCCURRED ... DESPITE OPENING AND RESUSCITATION EFFORTS, THE PATIENT EXPIRED IN THE OPERATING ROOM.
spotlight.label: Death filed under the stapler instrument; the recalled reload 48230M is only in the text.

extraction.one_line: A SUREFORM 30 stapler fired with a gray reload failed to deploy staples, causing massive bleeding and patient death.

next_steps: Read every death in the wider Intuitive stapler set for a reload named only in the narrative.
Match report 2955842-2026-01596 against the 11 Mar 2026 recall lot and date.
Re-pull GDW and NAY for new 8 mm SureForm reports since the recall.
cannot_show: MAUDE reports are unvalidated and carry no denominator (units sold or procedures), so they can never give a rate.
Before 2019 many stapler reports were filed as Alternative Summary Reports outside public MAUDE, so pre-2019 counts are undercounts.
Manufacturer reports include follow-ups and supplements, so a count of reports is not a count of patients.
Whether report 2955842-2026-01596 is the death FDA cites in the 11 Mar 2026 recall is not confirmed; it is consistent with it.

findings.title: Recalled lots named in reports before the maker's letter — Echelon VASECR35
findings.device: Ethicon Endopath Echelon Vascular White Reload (VASECR35)
findings.headline: 28 of 57 recalled lots were already in the reports
findings.brief: FDA’s 22 April 2025 correction for VASECR35 identified 57 affected lots, of which 28 appear in MAUDE reports covering 89 total reports. Fourteen of those reports arrived before the correction letter, the earliest dated 2024‑12‑17, including a death reported as 3005075853‑2025‑02636 on lot 326D66, which quotes “THE STAPLES FELL BY OPENING THE STAPLING AND THERE WAS LEAKAGE … THE PATIENT EXPIRED.” Lockout‑type narratives were two or fewer per year from 2016 through 2024 and rose to 59 in 2025.

spotlight.quote: THE STAPLES FELL BY OPENING THE STAPLING AND THERE WAS LEAKAGE ... THE PATIENT EXPIRED.
spotlight.label: A death on lot 326D66, received 12 days before Ethicon's correction letter named that lot.

next_steps: Alert on any report whose lot is on an FDA correction list but received before the letter.
Review the 14 pre-letter reports on matched lots for a common failure mode.
Hold the lockout cluster as a watch item, not a signal, until volume or harm rises.
cannot_show: MAUDE reports are unvalidated and carry no denominator (units sold or procedures), so they can never give a rate.
Before 2019 many stapler reports were filed as Alternative Summary Reports outside public MAUDE, so pre-2019 counts are undercounts.
Manufacturer reports include follow-ups and supplements, so a count of reports is not a count of patients.
A lot named in a report is not proof that the lot caused the harm.
Reports name 28 of the 57 lots; the other 29 may simply not have been reported, not that they were safe.

findings.title: The code trap — deaths filed under the staple code, not the stapler
findings.device: All surgical staplers & staples (product codes GAG, GDW)
findings.headline: 404 of 412 deaths were under the staple code — GAG shows 278, GDW shows 1103
findings.brief: According to the FDA’s 2019 panel analysis, of the 412 deaths reported for stapler‑staple events between 2011 and 2018, 404 were coded under the staple code (GDW) and only 8 under the stapler code (GAG). Current MAUDE data show the stapler code (GAG) associated with 278 death reports while the staple code (GDW) has 1103 death reports. Malfunction reports for surgical staplers increased from 3,843 in 2016 to 10,023 in 2017 and 12,951 in 2018 after the Alternative Summary Reporting exemption ended, and the FDA reclassified internal‑use surgical staplers from class I to class II with special controls in 2021 (86 FR 56195).

spotlight.quote: 404 of 412 deaths were reported under the staple product code, not the stapler product code.
spotlight.label: The split is FDA's own finding; Lot Watch pulls GDW and NAY, not just GAG.

next_steps: Always pull the staple code (GDW) and the robotic code (NAY) alongside the stapler code (GAG).
Treat a death under a staple or component code as a stapler death for clustering.
Flag any device whose deaths sit disproportionately under a component code.
cannot_show: MAUDE reports are unvalidated and carry no denominator (units sold or procedures), so they can never give a rate.
Before 2019 many stapler reports were filed as Alternative Summary Reports outside public MAUDE, so pre-2019 counts are undercounts.
Manufacturer reports include follow-ups and supplements, so a count of reports is not a count of patients.
The 2011-2018 figures are FDA's; the 51% filed as summary reports were not in public MAUDE for pre-2017 years at all.

findings.title: Circular stapler CDH29A — reports clustered by failure mode
findings.device: Ethicon Proximate ILS Curved Intraluminal Stapler (CDH29A)
findings.headline: 300 reports sorted into 8 failure modes by reading the text
findings.brief: The 300 MAUDE reports on the Ethicon circular stapler CDH29A were categorized by failure mode as follows: 84 incomplete staple line, 80 other, 41 no staples formed, 35 lockout/would not fire, 33 misfire, 15 not stated, 9 staple/fragment left, and 3 uncut or retained washer (300 reports). CDH29A is the device family subject to Ethicon’s 11 April 2019 Class I recall of 92,496 units for insufficient firing and failure to completely form staples. In Hershberger v. Ethicon (S.D. W. Va. 2011), a CDH29 stapler cut tissue but fired no staples; Ethicon’s initial search used only the “missing staples” complaint code, while a later search for “would not staple” identified 125 additional incidents, 44 of which were deemed similar by the plaintiffs, and the court imposed $53,350.36 in discovery sanctions without finding bad faith or ruling on liability.

spotlight.quote: Ethicon searched one complaint code ("missing staples") and not "would not staple"; later searches under that code turned up 125 more incidents, of which plaintiffs counted 44 as similar. The magistrate judge called the first response "unreasonable in the extreme and, frankly, nonsensical."
spotlight.label: Similar reports sat under a different complaint code and were not searched at first — the gap Lot Watch closes by reading the text.

next_steps: Cluster the insufficient-firing and uncut-washer reports against the 2019 Class I recall.
Treat "would not staple" and "missing staples" as one failure mode, not two codes.
Carry the Hershberger coding lesson into every complaint-database search.
cannot_show: MAUDE reports are unvalidated and carry no denominator (units sold or procedures), so they can never give a rate.
Before 2019 many stapler reports were filed as Alternative Summary Reports outside public MAUDE, so pre-2019 counts are undercounts.
Manufacturer reports include follow-ups and supplements, so a count of reports is not a count of patients.
This is a 300-report sample (received April 2020 to August 2021) of about 2,548 CDH29A reports; the mix of failure modes may shift across the full set.
Hershberger's merits outcome is not verified; the $53,350.36 is a discovery sanction, not a liability finding.

findings.title: No device to examine — stapler & staple deaths, 2024-25
findings.device: All stapler & staple death reports, 2024-2025 (GAG, GDW)
findings.headline: device not available for evaluation in 125 of 144 death reports
findings.brief: Among the 144 stapler‑staple death reports received in 2024‑2025 (codes GAG and GDW), the manufacturer’s record indicated that the device was not available for evaluation in 125 cases. A keyword search of all 144 narratives identified leak or dehiscence in 70 reports and bleeding in 65 reports, and when the device was unavailable the narrative served as the primary account of failure. The reports were distributed by manufacturer as 75 Covidien/Medtronic, 51 Ethicon/J&J, and 18 Intuitive.

spotlight.quote: In 125 of 144 stapler/staple death reports, the device was recorded as not available for evaluation.
spotlight.label: When the device is gone, the only record of what failed is the narrative — which is what Lot Watch reads.

next_steps: Prioritise narrative extraction for deaths where the device was not available.
Track, per maker, how often the device is unavailable for evaluation.
Use the narrative failure mode when no failure analysis exists.
cannot_show: MAUDE reports are unvalidated and carry no denominator (units sold or procedures), so they can never give a rate.
Before 2019 many stapler reports were filed as Alternative Summary Reports outside public MAUDE, so pre-2019 counts are undercounts.
Manufacturer reports include follow-ups and supplements, so a count of reports is not a count of patients.
"Not available for evaluation" is the manufacturer's own field; it does not say why the device was unavailable.
Maker buckets are by the reporting-manufacturer field and may group related corporate entities.
